nodes.norm_label: this is referred to as ‘trimming the load’ and is enforced via a vehicle blueprint/load configuration spec that lfg provides to clients\.

nodes.label: The system should ensure that the consolidated load does not exceed the vehicle’s maximum legal weight\.

nodes.label: All fines and recovery costs arising from incorrect loading are passed back to the loading client \(e\.g\. FedEx\), as they are responsible for adhering to LFG’s load configuration blueprint\.
nodes.norm_label: all fines and recovery costs arising from incorrect loading are passed back to the loading client \(e\.g\. fedex\), as they are responsible for adhering to lfg’s load configuration blueprint\.

nodes.label: Loading is FedEx’s responsibility\. LFG provides them with the vehicle blueprint \(including high\-canopy configurations for volumetric freight\), and FedEx must load accordingly\.
nodes.norm_label: loading is fedex’s responsibility\. lfg provides them with the vehicle blueprint \(including high\-canopy configurations for volumetric freight\), and fedex must load accordingly\.

nodes.label: It is in the client’s financial interest to comply with the load configuration, as non\-compliance costs fall on them\.
nodes.norm_label: it is in the client’s financial interest to comply with the load configuration, as non\-compliance costs fall on them\.

nodes.label: Confirmed: the system must be designed to accommodate multiple clients on a single truck\. This is standard practice for break bulk / break box services\.
nodes.norm_label: confirmed: the system must be designed to accommodate multiple clients on a single truck\. this is standard practice for break bulk / break box services\.

nodes.label: Example: a truck departing Durban may carry loads from FedEx, Courier Guy, Seaborne, and others simultaneously\.
nodes.norm_label: example: a truck departing durban may carry loads from fedex, courier guy, seaborne, and others simultaneously\.

nodes.label: LFG Durban manifests all clients onto one vehicle internally; this manifest is communicated LFG Durban → LFG Johannesburg \(not to the driver\)\.
nodes.norm_label: lfg durban manifests all clients onto one vehicle internally; this manifest is communicated lfg durban → lfg johannesburg \(not to the driver\)\.

nodes.label: Loading order is determined by urgency, yield, and client priority\. For example, a more urgent FedEx load is placed at the door \(unloaded first on arrival\), while a lower\-priority Courier Guy load is placed at the bulkhead \(driver\-side, rear of load body\)\.
nodes.norm_label: loading order is determined by urgency, yield, and client priority\. for example, a more urgent fedex load is placed at the door \(unloaded first on arrival\), while a lower\-priority courier guy load is placed at the bulkhead \(driver\-side, rear of load body\)\.

nodes.label: This operational priority logic should be accessible to the dispatcher in FreightProof\.
nodes.norm_label: this operational priority logic should be accessible to the dispatcher in freightproof\.

nodes.label: Scheduled Break Bulk Service: Clients bring their shipments to the LFG facility\. LFG consolidates and loads the truck according to priority and weight rules\.
nodes.norm_label: scheduled break bulk service: clients bring their shipments to the lfg facility\. lfg consolidates and loads the truck according to priority and weight rules\.

nodes.label: Ad Hoc Collection Service: The truck travels to individual client sites to collect loads \(e\.g\. collect 3 tonnes from FedEx, then continue to Courier Guy for 4 tonnes\)\. This is a secondary, on\-request service\.
nodes.norm_label: ad hoc collection service: the truck travels to individual client sites to collect loads \(e\.g\. collect 3 tonnes from fedex, then continue to courier guy for 4 tonnes\)\. this is a secondary, on\-request service\.

nodes.label: The system must therefore support multiple pickup locations and multiple drop\-off points per trip\.
nodes.norm_label: the system must therefore support multiple pickup locations and multiple drop\-off points per trip\.

nodes.label: Return legs must be tracked distinctly from outbound trips\. If the vehicle returns empty, that cost is absorbed by LFG, making it important for management to have visibility\.
nodes.norm_label: return legs must be tracked distinctly from outbound trips\. if the vehicle returns empty, that cost is absorbed by lfg, making it important for management to have visibility\.

nodes.label: LFG actively tries to find return loads to minimise empty\-leg costs\.
nodes.norm_label: lfg actively tries to find return loads to minimise empty\-leg costs\.

nodes.label: Tracking return legs also feeds into rotation planning \(i\.e\. ensuring a truck is available and positioned for the following night’s departing service\)\.
nodes.norm_label: tracking return legs also feeds into rotation planning \(i\.e\. ensuring a truck is available and positioned for the following night’s departing service\)\.

nodes.label: Design decision: the dispatcher should be able to either initiate a return leg as a continuation of an existing trip or create a new trip entry\. This still needs to be finalised in the system design\.
nodes.norm_label: design decision: the dispatcher should be able to either initiate a return leg as a continuation of an existing trip or create a new trip entry\. this still needs to be finalised in the system design\.

nodes.label: Parcel\-level tracking is very important\. A key use case is dispute resolution: if a client \(e\.g\. FedEx\) reports a missing parcel, LFG needs to determine whether the parcel was in their custody and, if so, at which point in the journey it left\.
nodes.norm_label: parcel\-level tracking is very important\. a key use case is dispute resolution: if a client \(e\.g\. fedex\) reports a missing parcel, lfg needs to determine whether the parcel was in their custody and, if so, at which point in the journey it left\.

nodes.label: FreightProof’s ability to search a specific parcel reference and trace it through loading events, in\-transit checkpoints, and delivery handshakes was confirmed as a significant capability gap in the current market\.
nodes.norm_label: freightproof’s ability to search a specific parcel reference and trace it through loading events, in\-transit checkpoints, and delivery handshakes was confirmed as a significant capability gap in the current market\.

nodes.label: In practice, FedEx consolidates multiple parcels onto wooden pallets \(e\.g\. 50 parcels per pallet, shrink\-wrapped\)\. LFG receives these as single units\.
nodes.norm_label: in practice, fedex consolidates multiple parcels onto wooden pallets \(e\.g\. 50 parcels per pallet, shrink\-wrapped\)\. lfg receives these as single units\.

nodes.label: LFG therefore cannot track at individual parcel level — only at the consolidated unit/pallet level\.
nodes.norm_label: lfg therefore cannot track at individual parcel level — only at the consolidated unit/pallet level\.

nodes.label: FreightProof should track at the unit level \(i\.e\. the pallet or consolidated shipment handed to LFG\), not at the individual parcel level\. FedEx’s internal systems \(Parcel Perfect\) hold the parcel\-to\-pallet mapping\.
nodes.norm_label: freightproof should track at the unit level \(i\.e\. the pallet or consolidated shipment handed to lfg\), not at the individual parcel level\. fedex’s internal systems \(parcel perfect\) hold the parcel\-to\-pallet mapping\.

nodes.label: Example: a 10\-pallet shipment may contain parcels from multiple FedEx clients across different pallets\. LFG tracks each pallet as a unit\.
nodes.norm_label: example: a 10\-pallet shipment may contain parcels from multiple fedex clients across different pallets\. lfg tracks each pallet as a unit\.
